# user-defined-patterns (KPT*)

**Pattern rules**

This rule is enabled by default.

## What it does

Checks every source file against regular expressions (Rust [`regex`](https://docs.rs/regex) syntax) defined in your project configuration, line by line. Each pattern has its own code and is addressable in `select`, `ignore`, `per-file-ignores` and `# noqa`.

## Why is this bad?

Some conventions are specific to a project (no bare `print()`, no `breakpoint()` left behind, no unticketed `TODO`). A pattern rule enforces them without writing a plugin.

## Example

```python
print("hello")   # KPT001, with the pattern below
```

Use instead:

```python
logger.info("hello")
```

## Defining patterns

```toml
[[tool.konform.lint.user-defined-patterns.rules]]
id      = "KPT001"
message = "Use the project logger instead of bare print()."
pattern = '^\s*print\s*\('
files   = ["src/**/*.py"]
level   = "warning"
```

Patterns are loaded from the first available source:

1. Inline `[[tool.konform.lint.user-defined-patterns.rules]]` in the config file.
2. `rules_file = "path"` in `[tool.konform.lint.user-defined-patterns]`.
3. `konform_patterns.toml`, auto-discovered next to the config file.
4. `konform_patterns.yaml` (legacy fallback).

A standalone file uses plain `[[rules]]` tables.

## Pattern entry fields

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | yes | Code shown in output and used for `# noqa` |
| `message` | yes | Human-readable description |
| `pattern` | yes | Regex, or a list of regexes (any match fires) |
| `files` | no | Glob filter; omitted means every file |
| `level` | no | `"error"` or `"warning"`; inherits the table's `level` |
| `help` | no | Guidance text shown with the violation |
| `multiline` | no | Match against the whole file instead of line by line |
| `replacement` | no | Replacement string (`$1`, `$2`, ... captures); makes the pattern fixable |
| `sub_rules` | no | Refinements overriding `message`/`help`; the first match wins |

## Sub-rules

Sub-rules refine the message and help for more specific matches. The first sub-rule whose pattern(s) match the already-flagged line wins.

```toml
[[rules]]
id      = "KPT901"
message = "os.environ found, discouraged in test code."
pattern = 'os\.environ'
sub_rules = [
{
pattern = ['os\.environ\.get\(', 'os\.environ\['],
message = "os.environ special_key access detected.",
help    = "Use the 'shared_fixture' fixture instead.",
},
]
```

With `[[rules.sub_rules]]` tables, each sub-rule belongs to the most recently declared `[[rules]]` entry.

## Fix behavior

A pattern with a `replacement` is fixable; patterns without one are report-only.

## Options

Configured in `[tool.konform.lint.user-defined-patterns]`.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `level` | `"warning" \| "error"` | `"warning"` | Default severity for patterns that don't set their own. |
| `rules_file` | `str` | unset | Load patterns from this file instead of auto-discovery. |
| `rules` | `array of tables` | `[]` | Inline pattern entries. |

## Suppression

```python
x = 1  # noqa: KPT001
x = 1  # noqa: KPT  (every KPT* rule)
```
